findings.location: Paragraph containing Psalm 8 (source and translation near "When I consider thy heavens... / Quando considero os teus céus...")
findings.source_quote: When I consider thy heavens, the work of thy fingers, the moon and the stars, which thou hast ordained; What is man, that thou art mindful of him? and the son of man, that thou visitest him? –Psalm 8:3-4.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct a small typo in the translated sentence: change "ai formaste" to "ali formaste" or simply "que formaste" so the Portuguese reads naturally and accurately: e.g. "...a lua e as estrelas que ali formaste; que é o homem... – Salmo 8:3‑4."
findings.translation_quote: Quando considero os teus céus, obra dos teus dedos, a lua e as estrelas que ai formaste; que é o homem, para que te lembres dele? e o filho do homem, para que o visites? – Salmo 8:3‑4.

findings.location: Paragraph containing Psalm 14 citation (source and translation near "The fool hath said in his heart...")
findings.source_quote: The fool hath said in his heart, There is no God… –Psalm 14:1.
findings.suggested_fix: Consider using a more common modern Portuguese rendering of the verb to improve fluency, for example: "Disse o tolo no seu coração: Não há Deus... – Salmo 14:1." The current "Dize o tolo" is archaic but not theologically different; this is stylistic.
findings.translation_quote: Dize o tolo no seu coração: Não há Deus… – Salmo 14:1.
